direct-join.comment: Raised from 280275 on 2026-08-19, +20137 (+7.18%), 2.01 inferences per answer row: a conjunctive match now finds every row BEFORE any output template runs. Prior: LOWERED on 2026-08-19, 1176259054 to 1099833305, -6.63% attributed by interleaved A/B of one change: Expr writes its two slots through their own descriptors instead of object.__setattr__, which resolves the attribute NAME against the type on every call. Measured in isolation, object.__setattr__ costs 951 instructions against the descriptor's 568 over 200,000 writes, minimum of three runs. This lane builds five expressions per term and crosses none of them, so it is the workload where construction is the whole cost and the two writes per Expr are 12% of it.

typed-call.instruction_noise_comment: RAISED to 5.0 on 2026-08-17, from the 1.0 every other bench carries, because this workload's instruction count is LAYOUT-sensitive at 3.13% and nothing in the tree selects the mode. Ten clauses that NOTHING CALLS, appended to engine/python.pl, moved it from 6590121734 to 6390136042, and removing them moved it back. A sweep of the same probe reads 6590121734, 6558144686, 6462134810, 6518142057, 6438133781, 6390136042 at 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 clauses, saturating there and unchanged at 20, so it is a continuum rather than the two modes alpha-unique had [measured 2026-08-17]. The INFERENCE count is identical across every one of them, which is what says no logical work ever changed. This is code-layout bias, the effect Mytkowicz, Diwan, Hauswirth and Sweeney measured in 'Producing Wrong Data Without Doing Anything Obviously Wrong!' (ASPLOS 2009), where link order and environment size alone move a benchmark by several percent and can reverse a conclusion. alpha-unique's warm-up does NOT fix this one: with typed-call added to pure.py's _WARM_UP the same two trees still measure 6591481484 and 6391492325, so the mode is not the one-time stack growth that was, and the warm-up was reverted rather than left in for nothing. The allowance is measured rather than guessed, and the ceiling still sees what it exists for: this bench is gated in instructions because the inference counter cannot see the type-check specialisation, and disabling that specialisation by one token measures 9368378515, +42.2% against a 3.13% noise floor, a 13x margin [measured 2026-08-17]. The baseline stays at the LOW end of the layout range rather than being re-recorded at the tree's current value, so a real regression sitting on top of the high mode still fails.

wire-codec.comment: RAISED on 2026-08-19, 3457164978 to 3467063880, +0.286%, from Expr's lazy _wire slot on a workload that now CHAINS its trips. The workload changed in the same commit and the change is the honest half of that number: it used to re-encode one long-lived atom 2000 times, which the new slot answers from cache after the first, and the lane reported -31.61% for a change that stopped encoding rather than encoding faster. Each trip now encodes the atom the previous trip decoded, so encoding stays cold and the +0.286% is the slot's real cost on a cold crossing. Prior: LOWERED on 2026-08-19, 3522689581 to 3457054691. Same change as term-operators: Expr writes its slots through their descriptors. Attributed by interleaved A/B, 3536110132 to 3457065051, -2.24%. from_wire builds one Expr per decoded node, so this lane pays the two writes 51 times per trip.
